SPECIAL NUMBER SET HIERARCHY
                      
   $$\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbb{C}$$
   
   ├── $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ (Natural Numbers / Positive Integers)
   ├── $\mathbb{Z} = \{\dots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ (Integers)
   ├── $\mathbb{Q} = \left\{\frac{p}{q} \;\middle|\; p, q \in \mathbb{Z}, q \neq 0, \gcd(p,q)=1\right\}$ (Rational Numbers)
   └── $\mathbb{R} = \mathbb{Q} \cup \mathbb{I}$ (Real Numbers = Rationals $\cup$ Irrationals)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 3.1 The Empty Set, Universal Set, and Finitude
- **Empty Set (Null / Void Set, $\emptyset$ or $\{\}$)**: The unique set containing no elements. $\forall x, x \notin \emptyset$. Cardinality: $|\emptyset| = 0$.
- **Universal Set ($U$ or $\Omega$)**: A contextual master set containing all possible objects under consideration in a given analytical scope.
- **Finite vs. Infinite Sets**:
  - A set $A$ is **Finite** if there exists a bijection $f: A \to \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}_0$. The integer $n = |A|$ is the Cardinality.
  - Otherwise, $A$ is **Infinite** (e.g., $\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Equality and Inclusion (Subsets)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Equality and Inclusion (Subsets)
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Equal Sets ($A = B$)**: $A = B \iff (\forall x, x \in A \iff x \in B) \iff (A \subseteq B \text{ and } B \subseteq A)$
- **Subset ($A \subseteq B$)**: $A \subseteq B \iff (\forall x, x \in A \implies x \in B)$
- **Proper Subset ($A \subsetneq B$)**: $A \subsetneq B \iff (A \subseteq B \text{ and } \exists y \in B \text{ such that } y \notin A)$

#### Fundamental Theorem on the Empty Set:
The empty set $\emptyset$ is a subset of every set $A$.
*Proof*: The statement $\emptyset \subseteq A \iff (\forall x, x \in \emptyset \implies x \in A)$. Since $x \in \emptyset$ is false for all $x$, the material implication $(F \implies P)$ is vacuously true. $\blacksquare$
